subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB323, LANDED. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.27.4 'insufficient authority exists to open the file': OK, 3)): 'If the file associated with file-name-1 is present and insufficient authority exists to open the file, the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, and the I-O status value in the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is set to \'37\''. The status is §9.1.13.6 6) b) (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'insufficient authority exists to access the file': OK) — 'A permanent error exists because an OPEN statement or DELETE FILE statement is attempted on a file and insufficient authority exists to access the file. The ability to detect this is processor dependent.' WAS: every OpenCore decided presence with File.Exists, which swallows every access error and answers false, so a PRESENT-but-refused file classified as ABSENT and never reached the '37' mapping. Probed on a worktree build at 000b6242 (a file under a directory whose DACL denies the running user, icacls /deny :(RX)): non-optional sequential OPEN INPUT = '35'; SELECT OPTIONAL over the same path = '05' — a SUCCESSFUL open — with the first READ reporting AT END '10'; relative and indexed non-optional OPEN INPUT = '35'. NOW: the presence question has ONE site and THREE answers — HostFile.Probe (IO/FileSupport.cs) returns FilePresence.Absent / Present / Unauthorized from File.GetAttributes, whose FAILURES distinguish a missing file (FileNotFoundException / DirectoryNotFoundException → §9.1.13.6 5)'s '35') from a refused one (UnauthorizedAccessException → GR3's '37'); every other IOException propagates so §9.1.13.6 1)'s '30' stays mapped in one place. FileConnector.Open takes that probe ONCE per OPEN, answers GR3 from it, and hands the result to OpenCore(mode, presence), so no organization re-asks the host and no two probes in one statement can disagree. The same probe now serves §14.9.10.4 GR14/GR16 in FileRegistry.DeleteFile, which had carried the only correct copy of the rule since kb/Work PB140 (this row was the OPEN arm of that two-arm dispatch, unfixed for five months). RE-PROBED after the fix on the same denied path: sequential non-optional '37', sequential OPTIONAL '37', relative non-optional '37', indexed non-optional '37'; a genuinely ABSENT file inside the same denied directory still answers '35', so the probe does not over-fire. OUTPUT IS DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THE SHORT-CIRCUIT and that is required, not a convenience: GR18 makes OUTPUT a creation that never consults presence, §9.1.13.6 5) is defined only 'for an OPEN statement with the INPUT, I-O, or EXTEND phrase', and a directory the process may write but not list legitimately accepts a NEW file (measured: create OK, truncate-existing UnauthorizedAccessException) — so a blanket '37' would reject an OPEN OUTPUT the operating environment carries out. An OUTPUT over a present-and-refused file still reaches '37' through the creating stream's own exception and Open's catch. COVERING TESTS: unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests establishes the GR3 precondition for real (a DACL deny ACE on Windows, mode 000 on Unix) and verifies the denial with a raw File.OpenRead rather than with the subject under test — the conformance runner compiles a .cob and compares output with nowhere to express 'first make this file unreadable', so no golden can reach this arm; its GR3 assertions were shown to FAIL (8 of them) with the short-circuit disabled. conformance:cases/9.1.13.6-Permanent-error-condition-with-unsuccessful-completion/pb323_open_presence_arms pins the probe's OTHER two answers — Absent and Present across all three organizations and both OPTIONAL states, expected values derived from §9.1.13.6 5) ('35'), §14.9.27.4 13) + Table 18 ('05' then §9.1.13.4 1)'s at-end '10') and §14.9.27.4 17) (an absent OPTIONAL EXTEND is created, '05') — because a refactor that got Absent wrong would be louder than the defect it fixed. unit:HostFileProbeDriftTests keeps the probe singular: File.Exists, .Exists and File.GetAttributes are banned everywhere under Runtime/IO but FileSupport.cs (it flags all 10 pre-fix sites at 000b6242, including the var-named FileInfo the first draft of its regex missed). || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 — GR3's explicit '37' sentence is the 2023 clarification (Annex E.2 item 18, 'The OPEN statement may return a file status \'37\' for insufficient authority to open a file'), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md §3 determines it is emitted at EVERY edition and not gated, so the rule is adjudicated at all four.
